scenario: 召回(retrieval)用双塔 ANN 从数十亿视频里选出几百个候选，接下来要决定最终展示顺序。
scenario_en: Retrieval uses a two-tower ANN to pull a few hundred candidates from billions of videos; now you must decide the final display order.
q: 推荐漏斗里排序(ranking)层的定位是什么？
q_en: What is the role of the ranking layer in the recommendation funnel?
why: 排序是精排层：候选已被压到几百个，这里能负担多目标精算，在观看时长、满意度、新鲜度、多样性之间平衡，不让任何单一目标独大。
why_en: Ranking is the precision layer that scores a few hundred candidates against competing objectives (watch time, satisfaction, freshness, diversity) so none dominates.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["召回 retrieval
双塔 ANN·数十亿→几百"] --> K["排序 ranking
多目标精排"] K --> RR["重排 re-ranking
多样性+政策"]
options: 召回层：从数十亿视频粗筛候选，追求高召回率和吞吐，不做精细排序
精排层：对几百个候选按多个竞争目标打分排序
只按预测观看时长单一分数排序，越长排越前，不看其它目标
存储视频 embedding 索引的服务层，供在线相似度查询
options_en: The retrieval layer: coarse-filter candidates from billions, optimizing recall and throughput, no fine ordering.
The precision layer: score a few hundred candidates against several competing objectives.
Rank purely by a single predicted-watch-time score, longer first, ignoring other objectives.
A serving layer that stores the video embedding index for online similarity lookups.
optionExplanations: 召回是上一层，负责从数十亿里粗筛；排序拿到的是它的几百个输出，做的是精排不是粗筛。
对；候选已被压小，排序才有算力上多目标精排，平衡竞争目标是它存在的理由。
单目标只是一种(坏的)排序策略，不是排序层的定位；排序恰恰要避免单一目标独大。
存 embedding 索引是召回侧 ANN 的事，排序不负责建索引。
optionExplanations_en: Retrieval is the prior layer that coarse-filters from billions; ranking consumes its few-hundred output and does precision ordering, not filtering.
Correct — with candidates already shrunk, ranking can afford multi-objective precision scoring; balancing competing goals is its whole reason to exist.
Single-objective is just one (bad) ranking policy, not the layer's definition; ranking exists precisely to stop one objective dominating.
Holding the embedding index is the retrieval-side ANN's job; ranking does not build indexes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐第一阶段：从海量物料里快速选出几百个候选，追求召回率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retrieval is stage one: quickly select a few hundred candidates from a huge corpus, optimizing recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻搜索，在向量空间里快速找相似 embedding，不保证精确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search quickly finds similar embeddings in vector space without guaranteeing exactness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户塔和物料塔各自独立编码 embedding，用内积算相似度，适合上亿规模召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model encodes user and item into separate embeddings and scores by dot product, suited to billion-scale retrieval.

scenario: 有人提议排序器只用「预测观看时长」一个分数，观看越久排越前。
scenario_en: Someone proposes a ranker driven by a single predicted-watch-time score: the longer the watch, the higher it ranks.
q: 只优化观看时长这一个目标会导致什么后果？
q_en: What does optimizing watch time alone lead to?
why: 单目标会过拟合到自动播放兔子洞：模型学会推能拖住人的煽动性/标题党内容，观看时长涨但满意度掉、曝光被刷分内容占据。这正是最常见的单目标陷阱。
why_en: A single objective overfits into autoplay rabbit holes—sensational clickbait that keeps people watching while satisfaction drops and exposure gets gamed.
options: 模型会自动兼顾满意度和多样性，因为长观看通常等于高满意
只是训练变慢，但推荐质量和多目标排序没有区别
过拟合到自动播放兔子洞：推标题党内容、满意度掉
观看时长和满意度会一起上升，几乎没有代价，无需其它目标
options_en: The model automatically balances satisfaction and diversity, since long watches usually equal high satisfaction.
It only slows training, but recommendation quality is no different from multi-objective ranking.
It overfits into autoplay rabbit holes: clickbait gets pushed and satisfaction drops.
Watch time and satisfaction rise together at essentially no cost, so no other objective is needed.
optionExplanations: 长观看不等于满意——标题党能拖住人却让人后悔；单目标没有满意度信号去纠偏。
问题不在训练速度，而在优化目标错位，直接决定了推荐内容的质量走向。
对；观看时长是可被煽动内容套利的代理，缺满意度约束就会滑向兔子洞。
两者恰恰会背离(cannibalization)：YouTube 自己的研究证实纯参与度优化拉低了自报满意度。
optionExplanations_en: Long watches are not satisfaction—clickbait holds attention while leaving regret; a single objective has no satisfaction signal to correct it.
The issue is not training speed but a misaligned objective, which directly steers what content gets recommended.
Correct — watch time is a proxy that sensational content can arbitrage; without a satisfaction constraint it slides into rabbit holes.
The two actually diverge (cannibalization): YouTube's own research confirmed pure engagement optimization dropped self-reported satisfaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动播放不断推同类刺激内容，把用户越拖越深的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rabbit hole is when autoplay keeps pushing similar stimulating content, pulling the user ever deeper.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用夸张标题或封面骗点击，实际内容质量低的内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clickbait uses exaggerated titles or thumbnails to farm clicks while the actual content is low quality.

scenario: 要避免单目标陷阱，团队决定用一个共享 backbone 挂多个预测头。
scenario_en: To dodge the single-objective trap, the team uses one shared backbone feeding multiple prediction heads.
q: 多目标排序模型的共享 backbone 上通常挂哪些预测头？(多选)
q_en: Which prediction heads typically sit on a multi-objective ranker's shared backbone? (multiple)
why: 共享 backbone + 多头：P(click)抓即时兴趣、E[watch time|click]抓观看深度、P(like)/P(share)是满意度代理、P(not-dislike)过滤低质。每个头对应一个业务目标。
why_en: One shared backbone with heads for P(click), E[watch time | click], P(like)/P(share), and P(not-dislike)—each head maps to a business objective.
options: P(click)：即时兴趣
E[watch time | click]：点击后的观看深度
P(like) / P(share)：显式正反馈，满意度代理
P(bitrate)：预测视频编码码率高低
options_en: P(click): immediate interest.
E[watch time | click]: depth of engagement after a click.
P(like) / P(share): explicit positive feedback, a satisfaction proxy.
P(bitrate): predict the video's encoding bitrate.
optionExplanations: 对；点击概率是最直接的即时兴趣信号，是打分公式的第一项。
对；只知道点没点不够，还要预测点了会看多久，才反映真实吸引力。
对；点赞/转发是用户主动给的满意度代理，用来对冲纯观看时长。
错；码率是视频编码属性，与用户偏好无关，不会作为排序预测头。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — click probability is the most direct immediate-interest signal, the first term of the scoring formula.
Correct — knowing whether they clicked is not enough; predicting how long reflects true pull.
Correct — likes/shares are user-volunteered satisfaction proxies used to offset raw watch time.
Wrong — bitrate is a video encoding attribute, unrelated to user preference, never a ranking head.

termDefinitions.meaning: 共享网络之上一个小输出分支，专门预测某一个目标(如点击、点赞)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prediction head is a small output branch on top of the shared network that predicts one objective (e.g. click, like).

termDefinitions.meaning: 用可测的显式反馈(点赞、转发)近似难测的真实满意度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A satisfaction proxy uses measurable explicit feedback (likes, shares) to approximate hard-to-measure true satisfaction.

scenario: 多个预测头输出多个分数，最终要合成一个可排序的标量。
scenario_en: Multiple heads output multiple scores that must be combined into one sortable scalar.
q: 补全多目标标量化(scalarization)的打分与调权方式：
q_en: Fill in how multi-objective scalarization scores and tunes weights:
text: score = w1·P(click)·{{E[watch time]}} + w2·P(like) + w3·P(share) − w4·{{P(dislike)}}；权重不是常数，靠 {{在线 A/B}} 调，且按 {{surface}} 不同而变。
text_en: score = w1·P(click)·{{E[watch time]}} + w2·P(like) + w3·P(share) − w4·{{P(dislike)}}; weights are not constants—tuned by {{online A/B}} and varying by {{surface}}.
why: 标量化把多个目标分数用加权和压成一个标量来排序；点赞/转发加正权、不喜欢减负权。权重靠在线 A/B 调、随 surface 变，不是写死的常数。
why_en: Scalarization collapses multiple objective scores into one sortable scalar via a weighted sum; weights are tuned by online A/B and vary by surface rather than being fixed constants.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个目标分数用加权和合成单一标量分，以便统一排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scalarization combines multiple objective scores into a single scalar via a weighted sum so items can be ranked uniformly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一 App 里不同的推荐位(首页、Up Next、搜索页)，各自权重可不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A surface is a distinct recommendation slot (home, Up Next, search) that can carry its own weights.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分到对照/实验组，比较线上指标差异来选参数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users into control and treatment to compare live metrics and pick parameters.

scenario: 首页想要多样和新鲜，「Up Next(自动播放下一个)」想要观看连续性，两个 surface 共用同一批预测头。
scenario_en: The home feed wants diversity and freshness; 'Up Next' (autoplay) wants watch continuity; both surfaces share the same prediction heads.
q: 多目标标量化的权重该怎么设定？
q_en: How should the multi-objective scalarization weights be set?
why: 权重不是全局常数：最终分 = Σ wᵢ × pᵢ(第 i 个目标的预测)，w 按 surface 标定再用在线 A/B 调——首页偏多样/新鲜，Up Next 偏观看连续性。
why_en: Weights are not global constants: the final score is a weighted sum of per-objective predictions, and the weights are calibrated per surface and tuned by online A/B — home leans diversity and freshness, Up Next leans watch continuity.
tradeoff: 按 surface 分别调权(贴合各位置目标) vs 全局一套常数(简单但错配)
options: 用一套全局常数权重，所有 surface 通用，改动少也好维护
按 surface 分别设权重，并用在线 A/B 调优
让模型自己在推理时随机选权重，增加输出多样性
只保留观看时长一项权重，其余目标权重全设 0 以简化
options_en: Use one set of global constant weights for all surfaces—fewer changes, easy to maintain.
Set weights per surface and tune them with online A/B tests.
Let the model pick weights randomly at inference time to add output variety.
Keep only the watch-time weight and set all other objective weights to 0 for simplicity.
whenOtherWins: 若产品只有单一 surface、且流量不足以跑可信 A/B，可先用一套人工设定的权重起步，等有量再分化。
optionExplanations: 全局常数忽略了各 surface 目标不同：Up Next 和首页想要的东西根本不一样，一刀切会错配。
对；权重是产品杠杆，随位置和用户分群变，用 A/B 找到每个 surface 的最优点。
随机权重不可复现、无法优化，只会让线上指标抖动，不是「多样性」手段。
把其它权重归零就退回了单目标兔子洞陷阱，正是要避免的。
optionExplanations_en: Global constants ignore that each surface has different goals: Up Next and home want different things, so one-size-fits-all misaligns.
Correct — weights are a product lever that varies by placement and user segment; A/B finds each surface's optimum.
Random weights are irreproducible and unoptimizable—just metric jitter, not a diversity mechanism.
Zeroing other weights reverts to the single-objective rabbit-hole trap, exactly what to avoid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按行为或人群切分的用户子集，可各自用不同权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A user segment is a behavior- or demographic-based subset of users that can carry its own weights.

scenario: 四个目标各自有收益，但过度加权任何一个都有独特的副作用。
scenario_en: Each of the four objectives has a benefit, but over-weighting any one carries a distinct side effect.
q: 把「过度加权某目标」和「它带来的风险」正确配对，哪一组是对的？
q_en: Which pairing of 'over-weighting an objective' to 'its risk' is correct?
why: 四目标各有过度加权的风险：观看时长→标题党/成瘾，满意度→参与量下降，新鲜度→质量稀释，多样性→相关性流失。命题就是要在它们之间权衡而非单极。
why_en: Each objective has an over-weighting risk: watch time→clickbait/addiction, satisfaction→lower engagement volume, freshness→quality dilution, diversity→relevance loss.
options: 过度加权多样性 → 成瘾/标题党
过度加权观看时长 → 质量稀释
过度加权满意度 → 参与量下降
过度加权新鲜度 → 相关性流失
options_en: Over-weighting diversity → addiction/clickbait.
Over-weighting watch time → quality dilution.
Over-weighting satisfaction → engagement volume drops.
Over-weighting freshness → relevance loss.
optionExplanations: 配错了：成瘾/标题党是过度加权观看时长的风险，多样性的风险是相关性流失。
配错了：质量稀释是过度加权新鲜度的风险(为新而新)；观看时长的风险是标题党/成瘾。
对；只追满意度会推更「温和」但没那么抓人的内容，总参与量随之下降。
配错了：相关性流失是过度加权多样性的风险；新鲜度过头的风险是质量稀释。
optionExplanations_en: Mispaired: addiction/clickbait is the watch-time over-weighting risk; diversity's risk is relevance loss.
Mispaired: quality dilution is freshness's over-weighting risk (new for its own sake); watch time's risk is clickbait/addiction.
Correct — chasing satisfaction alone surfaces milder, less gripping content, so total engagement volume falls.
Mispaired: relevance loss is diversity's over-weighting risk; over-doing freshness dilutes quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为追求新鲜把低质新内容也顶上来，拉低整体质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quality dilution is when chasing freshness surfaces low-quality new content and drags overall quality down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 算法只推同类内容，用户接触面越来越窄。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A filter bubble is when the algorithm keeps recommending similar content, narrowing what the user sees.

scenario: 双塔在召回阶段要独立给数十亿视频打分(用户塔、视频塔分开算内积)；到排序阶段只剩几百个候选。
scenario_en: The two-tower must score billions independently in retrieval (user and item towers dot-producted); by ranking only a few hundred candidates remain.
q: 为什么排序阶段能用丰富的 user×video 交叉特征，召回阶段却不能？
q_en: Why can ranking use rich user×video cross-features while retrieval cannot?
why: 候选数量级决定了特征能力：召回要在数十亿里打分，只能用可预计算的双塔独立向量；排序只面对几百个，才算得起显式交叉。
why_en: Candidate scale decides what features you can use: retrieval scores billions so it can only use precomputable two-tower vectors, while ranking sees a few hundred and can afford explicit crosses.
tradeoff: 双塔可扩展但禁交叉 vs 交叉特征强但只能算几百个
options: 排序只有几百候选，算得起 user×video 交叉；召回双塔只能独立编码
因为召回模型太小装不下交叉特征，换个更大的召回模型就能在数十亿上做交叉
因为交叉特征只对视频有用、对用户无用，所以放在离用户更近的排序层
因为排序不需要 embedding，纯用规则打分，所以能自由加特征
options_en: Ranking sees only hundreds of candidates so it can afford user×video crosses; the retrieval two-tower can only encode each side separately.
Because the retrieval model is too small for cross-features; a bigger retrieval model could cross at billion scale.
Because cross-features help videos but not users, so they belong in the ranking layer closer to the user.
Because ranking needs no embeddings and scores by pure rules, so it can add features freely.
whenOtherWins: 若某个交叉信号可预计算成物料侧或用户侧的静态特征(不依赖对方 ID)，就能下沉到召回塔里，不必等到排序。
optionExplanations: 对；差异来自候选规模而非模型好坏——量级一降到几百，两两组合的算力就负担得起了。
不是模型大小问题：数十亿×每个用户的交叉是组合爆炸，再大的模型也没法在线算完。
交叉特征恰恰是 user×video 的联合信号，说它对用户无用是误解。
排序照样重度使用 embedding，只是额外能加交叉；不是纯规则。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the difference comes from candidate scale, not model quality: once you are down to hundreds, pairwise combinations become affordable.
Not a model-size issue: crossing billions with every user is a combinatorial explosion no larger model can compute online.
Cross-features are exactly the joint user×video signal, so calling them useless for users is a misread.
Ranking still heavily uses embeddings and merely adds crosses on top; it is not pure rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由两个字段组合而成的特征(如 user_country×video_language)，捕捉联合信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross feature combines two fields (e.g. user_country×video_language) to capture a joint signal.

scenario: 排序模型选用 Wide & Deep(联合训练、共享损失)，两侧各司其职。
scenario_en: The ranker uses Wide & Deep (jointly trained, shared loss), each side with a distinct job.
q: Wide & Deep 里 wide 侧和 deep 侧各负责什么？
q_en: In Wide & Deep, what does the wide side vs the deep side each do?
why: Wide 侧是稀疏交叉积上的线性层，负责记忆(memorization)高价值组合(如 language match)；deep 侧是稠密 embedding 上的前馈网络，负责泛化(generalization)到没见过的组合。
why_en: The wide side is a linear layer over sparse cross-products for memorization of high-value combos; the deep side is a feedforward net over dense embeddings for generalization to unseen combos.
tradeoff: wide 记忆(精确命中已知组合) vs deep 泛化(推广到未见组合)
diagram:
flowchart TB I["输入特征"] --> W["Wide: 稀疏交叉积线性层
memorization"] I --> D["Deep: 稠密 embedding 前馈网络
generalization"] W --> S["联合输出
共享损失"] D --> S
options: wide 负责泛化到没见过的组合，deep 靠线性交叉记忆已知组合
wide 和 deep 是两个独立模型，各训各的、推理时投票
wide 用稀疏交叉积做记忆，deep 用稠密 embedding 做泛化
wide 处理图像特征，deep 处理文本特征，按模态分工
options_en: Wide generalizes to combinations never seen before, while deep memorizes known ones via linear crosses.
Wide and deep are two separate models trained independently that vote at inference.
Wide memorizes via sparse cross-products; deep generalizes via dense embeddings.
Wide handles image features and deep handles text features, split by modality.
optionExplanations: 说反了：线性交叉积是记忆，深网泛化；把两者对调就错了。
Wide & Deep 是联合训练、共享一个损失，不是独立投票的两个模型。
对；这正是设计动机——记忆抓已知高价值组合，泛化补未见组合，互补。
分工不是按模态而是按记忆 vs 泛化；模态融合是另一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: linear cross-products do memorization and the deep net generalizes; swapping them is wrong.
Wide & Deep is jointly trained on one shared loss, not two independent voting models.
Correct — that is the design intent: memorize known high-value combos, generalize to unseen ones, complementary.
The split is memorization vs generalization, not by modality; modality fusion is a separate concern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性 wide 侧记住训练里出现过的高价值特征组合，命中即用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memorization is the linear wide side storing high-value feature combos seen in training and firing on them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深网通过 embedding 把相似组合归纳，能对训练里没见过的组合给合理预测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Generalization is the deep net using embeddings to generalize to feature combos unseen in training.

scenario: 特征空间巨大且动态：上千万稀疏 ID、有价值的交叉组合天天变，专家没法手工枚举出哪些交叉重要。
scenario_en: The feature space is huge and dynamic: tens of millions of sparse IDs, valuable crosses change daily, and experts cannot hand-enumerate which crosses matter.
q: 该选 Wide & Deep 还是 DCN？
q_en: Should you pick Wide & Deep or DCN?
why: DCN 用 cross network 自动学 2 阶/3 阶乃至更高阶交叉，省掉手工枚举；当特征空间太大太动态、没法人工列交叉时，DCN 更合适。
why_en: DCN's cross network automatically learns 2nd/3rd/higher-order interactions, so when the feature space is too large and dynamic to enumerate crosses by hand, DCN fits better.
tradeoff: DCN 自动学高阶交叉(免枚举) vs Wide 手工交叉(可控但要专家枚举)
options: 选 Wide & Deep：手工把所有重要交叉枚举进 wide 侧就行，反正专家最懂
选 DCN：用 cross network 自动学高阶交叉，免去手工枚举巨大动态特征空间
两个都不行，只能退回双塔，不做任何交叉
选 Wide & Deep 但把 deep 侧删掉，只留 wide 线性层
options_en: Pick Wide & Deep: just hand-enumerate all important crosses into the wide side, since experts know best.
Pick DCN: its cross network learns high-order interactions automatically, avoiding manual enumeration of a huge dynamic feature space.
Neither works; fall back to two-tower with no crosses at all.
Pick Wide & Deep but delete the deep side, keeping only the wide linear layer.
whenOtherWins: 若专家能列出少数高价值交叉(如 user_country×video_language)，Wide & Deep 的 wide 侧直接记忆更省算力也更可控。
optionExplanations: 特征空间太大太动态时手工枚举跟不上，会漏掉当天才冒出来的高价值交叉。
对；cross network 每层≈原始输入与当前输出的外积+残差，自动学高阶交叉，正对巨大动态特征空间。
双塔不做交叉恰恰是排序要弥补的短板，退回去等于放弃精度。
删掉 deep 侧就失去了泛化能力，只剩记忆，未见组合会预测很差。
optionExplanations_en: When the feature space is too large and dynamic, hand-enumeration cannot keep up and misses crosses that appeared only today.
Correct — each cross layer ≈ outer product of the original input and current output plus a residual, learning high-order crosses automatically, exactly right for a huge dynamic space.
Two-tower's lack of crosses is precisely what ranking exists to fix; falling back gives up precision.
Deleting the deep side loses generalization, leaving only memorization, so unseen combos predict poorly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 cross network 层自动学习高阶特征交叉，替代手工枚举交叉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN (Deep & Cross Network) uses cross-network layers to learn high-order feature interactions automatically, replacing manual crosses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 堆叠的交叉层，每层做输入与当前输出的外积再加残差，逐层升阶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross network stacks layers that take an outer product of the input and current output plus a residual, raising the interaction order each layer.

scenario: DCN 用在有上千个稀疏 ID 的排序任务上，cross 层的权重矩阵很大，参数和算力吃紧。
scenario_en: DCN is used on a ranking task with thousands of sparse IDs; the cross-layer weight matrix is large and strains params and compute.
q: DCN-v2 相比 DCN 的关键改动是什么，买到了什么？
q_en: What is DCN-v2's key change over DCN, and what does it buy?
why: DCN-v2 把 cross 层权重矩阵做低秩(low-rank)分解，并用低秩交叉层的混合(mixture)：参数更少、算力更省，同时保住对上千稀疏 ID 的表达力。
why_en: DCN-v2 low-rank-decomposes the cross-layer weight matrix into a mixture of low-rank cross layers: fewer params and less compute while keeping expressiveness over thousands of sparse IDs.
options: 把 cross 层删掉只留 deep 侧，靠加深网络补交叉
低秩(low-rank)分解权重矩阵并混合低秩交叉层，省算力
把所有稀疏 ID 换成一个哈希桶，牺牲表达力换速度
改用手工枚举交叉，回到 Wide & Deep 的做法
options_en: Remove the cross layers and keep only the deep side, compensating by deepening the net.
Low-rank-decompose the cross weight matrix into a mixture of low-rank cross layers to save compute.
Replace all sparse IDs with a single hash bucket, trading expressiveness for speed.
Switch to hand-enumerated crosses, reverting to the Wide & Deep approach.
optionExplanations: 删 cross 层就丢了 DCN 的核心(自动高阶交叉)，加深 deep 侧补不回显式交叉。
对；低秩分解把大权重矩阵拆小，用低秩交叉层混合保住表达力，是省参数的关键。
把稀疏 ID 塞进一个桶会严重丢信息，不是 DCN-v2 的做法。
DCN-v2 恰恰是延续自动交叉、只优化参数，不是退回手工枚举。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping cross layers loses DCN's core (automatic high-order crosses); deepening the deep side cannot recover explicit crosses.
Correct — low-rank decomposition shrinks the big weight matrix and a mixture of low-rank cross layers preserves expressiveness, the key to fewer params.
Cramming sparse IDs into one bucket loses heavy information, not what DCN-v2 does.
DCN-v2 continues automatic crossing and only trims params; it does not revert to hand enumeration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个大矩阵近似成两个小矩阵之积，参数从 d² 降到 2dr(r≪d)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-rank approximates a large matrix as a product of two small ones, cutting params from d² to 2dr with r≪d.

scenario: 工程师想把排序模型打分最高的 top-N 原样直接展示给用户。
scenario_en: An engineer wants to serve the ranker's top-N scored list to users exactly as is.
q: 直接 serve 原始 top 分数列表会产生什么问题，因此需要什么？
q_en: What problems arise from serving the raw top-scored list, and what is therefore needed?
why: 纯按分数排会造成信息茧房、单调雷同、以及政策违规内容混入。所以要加一层重排(re-ranking)后处理：软约束做多样性、硬约束做政策合规。
why_en: Serving raw scores causes filter bubbles, monotony, and policy violations, so a re-ranking post-processing layer is needed—soft constraints for diversity, hard for policy.
options: 没有问题：分数最高就是最优展示，重排是多余的
只会稍微增加延迟，内容体验和加重排没有区别
会有茧房、雷同、违规内容，需重排做软/硬约束
会让召回率下降，需要回到召回层重新扩大候选集再排一次
options_en: No problem: highest score is optimal display, re-ranking is redundant.
It only adds a little latency; the experience is no different from adding re-ranking.
It causes filter bubbles, monotony and policy violations, so you need re-ranking with soft and hard constraints.
It lowers recall, requiring a return to retrieval to widen the candidate set and rank again.
optionExplanations: 最高分只优化了模型目标，没管多样性和政策，单看分数会翻车。
问题不是延迟而是体验和合规：茧房、雷同、违规内容都不是延迟能描述的。
对；这三类问题正对应重排的两类约束——软(多样性) + 硬(政策)后处理。
召回率是上游召回的事；原始 top 列表的问题在多样性和政策，不是召回不够。
optionExplanations_en: Highest score only optimizes the model objective, ignoring diversity and policy, so raw scores derail.
The issue is experience and compliance, not latency: bubbles, monotony, and violating content are not latency effects.
Correct — these three problems map to re-ranking's two constraint types: soft (diversity) plus hard (policy) post-processing.
Recall is an upstream retrieval concern; the raw top list's problems are diversity and policy, not insufficient recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序打分之后的后处理层，注入多样性并施加硬性政策过滤。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-ranking is a post-processing layer after scoring that injects diversity and applies hard policy filters.

scenario: 重排要同时处理「多样性」和「政策合规」两类需求，但它们的强制程度不同。
scenario_en: Re-ranking handles both diversity and policy compliance, but they differ in how absolute they are.
q: 重排里的软约束和硬约束有什么本质区别？
q_en: What is the essential difference between soft and hard constraints in re-ranking?
why: 软约束(多样性)可与分数权衡，用 MMR/标量化实现，允许被高相关性盖过；硬约束(政策合规)是不可协商的确定性过滤，模型分数无论多高都不能覆盖。
why_en: Soft constraints (diversity) trade off against score via MMR/scalarization and can be outweighed; hard constraints (policy) are non-negotiable deterministic filters that no score can override.
tradeoff: 软约束(可与分数权衡) vs 硬约束(确定性、分数不可覆盖)
options: 软约束和硬约束都靠给分数加权实现，只是权重大小不同
软约束是确定性过滤、硬约束可被高分覆盖
软约束(多样性)可被高分盖过；硬约束(政策)是确定性过滤
软约束只在离线训练用、硬约束只在离线用，都不进在线服务
options_en: Both soft and hard constraints work by weighting the score, differing only in weight magnitude.
Soft constraints are deterministic filters and hard constraints can be overridden by a high score.
Soft constraints (diversity) can be outweighed by score; hard constraints (policy) are deterministic filters.
Soft constraints are used only in offline training and hard only offline; neither reaches online serving.
optionExplanations: 硬约束不是加权：它必须一票否决，加权再大也可能被更高分盖过，不满足「绝不出现」。
说反了：确定性过滤是硬约束的特征，软约束才可被高分盖过。
对；关键区分在能否被模型分数覆盖——软的可以权衡，硬的绝不能被覆盖。
两者都在在线服务的重排阶段生效，不是离线专用。
optionExplanations_en: Hard constraints are not weighting: they must veto absolutely, and any weight can still be outscored, failing 'never appears'.
Backwards: deterministic filtering is the hard constraint's hallmark; only soft constraints can be outweighed.
Correct — the key distinction is whether a model score can override it: soft trades off, hard can never be overridden.
Both act in the online re-ranking stage; they are not offline-only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 偏好性目标(如多样性)，可与相关性分数权衡，不是绝对。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A soft constraint is a preference (e.g. diversity) that trades off against the relevance score, not absolute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不可协商的规则(如政策合规)，用确定性逻辑强制，模型分数不能覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hard constraint is a non-negotiable rule (e.g. policy compliance) enforced by deterministic logic that no model score can override.

scenario: 重排要在保持相关性的同时避免连续推很像的视频。
scenario_en: Re-ranking must keep relevance while avoiding a run of very similar videos.
q: MMR(Maximal Marginal Relevance)是怎么做多样化的？
q_en: How does MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) achieve diversification?
why: MMR 贪心地逐个挑下一项，用「相关性 − 与已选集合的相似度」打分：太像已选内容的会被惩罚，从而在相关和多样之间平衡。
why_en: MMR greedily picks the next item by 'relevance minus similarity to already-chosen', penalizing items too similar to what is selected, balancing relevance and diversity.
options: 逐个挑下一项，用相关性减去与已选的相似度打分
把所有候选随机打乱，用随机性制造多样
只保留每个类目分数最高的一个，其余全部丢弃
训练时给相似样本加权，推理时不做任何处理
options_en: Greedily pick the next item, scoring it as relevance minus similarity to what's already chosen.
Randomly shuffle all candidates, using randomness to create variety.
Keep only the single highest-scored item per category and discard the rest.
Up-weight similar samples during training and do nothing at inference.
optionExplanations: 对；MMR 的核心就是这条边际收益公式，贪心地在相关性和与已选的差异之间权衡。
随机打乱破坏相关性，不是有控制的多样化，MMR 恰恰要保住相关性。
每类只留一个太激进会大量丢相关内容；MMR 是惩罚不是硬性去重。
多样化是在线重排的推理期动作，训练加权解决不了「本次列表太雷同」。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — MMR's core is this marginal-gain formula, greedily trading relevance against difference from what is chosen.
Random shuffle destroys relevance and is not controlled diversification; MMR keeps relevance.
Keeping one per category is too aggressive and drops relevant items; MMR penalizes rather than hard-dedupes.
Diversification is an inference-time re-ranking action; training-time weighting cannot fix 'this list is too samey'.

termDefinitions.meaning: 贪心重排法，按相关性减去与已选集合的相似度来逐项挑选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) is a greedy re-ranking method that picks items by relevance minus similarity to the already-chosen set.

scenario: 两种多样化算法都想让最终列表更分散，但机制不同。
scenario_en: Two diversification algorithms both spread out the final list, but by different mechanisms.
q: 多样化里 MMR 和 DPP(行列式点过程)的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between MMR and DPP (Determinantal Point Process) for diversity?
why: MMR 是贪心逐项挑选、显式用相关性减相似度；DPP 是概率模型，给「整体更不相似的子集」更高被选中概率，从集合层面建模多样性。
why_en: MMR is greedy per-item, explicitly relevance-minus-similarity; DPP is a probabilistic model that assigns higher probability to more dissimilar whole subsets, modeling diversity at the set level.
tradeoff: MMR 贪心逐项(简单直观) vs DPP 概率集合级(全局多样但更重)

rows: 相关性−相似度 贪心
概率给不相似子集更高概率

options: MMR 是概率集合模型，DPP 是贪心逐项挑选
两者完全等价，只是学术圈和工业界叫法不同
MMR 贪心逐项挑；DPP 用概率建模整个子集
MMR 用于硬性政策过滤，DPP 用于训练损失
options_en: MMR is a probabilistic set model and DPP is greedy per-item picking.
They are exactly equivalent, just named differently in academia and industry.
MMR picks greedily item by item; DPP models the whole subset probabilistically.
MMR is for hard policy filtering and DPP is for the training loss.
optionExplanations: 说反了：贪心逐项是 MMR，概率集合模型是 DPP。
机制不同：一个贪心逐项、一个概率建模整个子集，不是同一算法换名。
对；关键区分是粒度——MMR 一项一项挑，DPP 直接对整个子集的多样性建概率。
两者都是软性多样化手段，不做硬政策过滤，也不是训练损失。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: greedy per-item is MMR; the probabilistic set model is DPP.
The mechanisms differ: one greedy per-item, one probabilistic over whole subsets, not the same algorithm renamed.
Correct — the key distinction is granularity: MMR picks item by item, DPP models the diversity of the whole subset probabilistically.
Both are soft diversification tools, not hard policy filters or a training loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种概率模型，用行列式度量子集内部多样性，给更不相似的子集更高概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DPP (Determinantal Point Process) is a probabilistic model that uses a determinant to measure within-subset diversity, favoring more dissimilar subsets.

scenario: YouTube/TikTok 想保证每屏都出现一些新创作者或小众类目，而不是全被热门霸屏。
scenario_en: YouTube/TikTok want to guarantee each screen shows some new creators or niche categories rather than all popular content.
q: slot-based diversity(槽位多样性)是怎么保证多样性的？
q_en: How does slot-based diversity guarantee variety?
why: 槽位多样性预留固定 feed 位置给欠代表的类目或新创作者，是一种确定性配额，保证它们一定出现，而不是靠软打分去竞争。
why_en: Slot-based diversity reserves fixed feed positions for underrepresented categories or new creators—a deterministic quota that guarantees they appear rather than competing on soft score.
options: 训练时给小众类目样本加权，推理时不干预
预留固定 feed 位置给欠代表类目/新创作者
把所有候选按相似度聚类后只留每簇一个
对整个列表做概率采样，让分散子集概率更高
options_en: Up-weight niche-category samples in training and never intervene at inference.
Reserve fixed feed slots for underrepresented categories and new creators.
Cluster all candidates by similarity and keep only one per cluster.
Probabilistically sample the whole list so dispersed subsets are more likely.
optionExplanations: 训练加权改变不了单次列表的位置分配，也不保证欠代表内容一定出现。
对；槽位是确定性配额，直接把位置留出来，强保证曝光，不靠打分竞争。
按簇只留一个是去重不是留位；槽位是主动预留位置给特定群体。
概率采样是 DPP 的思路，不是槽位；槽位是确定性的位置预留。
optionExplanations_en: Training-time weighting cannot change position allocation in a single list nor guarantee underrepresented content appears.
Correct — slots are a deterministic quota that carves out positions, hard-guaranteeing exposure rather than competing on score.
Keeping one per cluster is dedup, not reservation; slots proactively reserve positions for a specific group.
Probabilistic sampling is the DPP idea, not slots; slots are deterministic position reservations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 feed 里预留固定位置给欠代表类目或新创作者的确定性配额法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Slot-based diversity is a deterministic quota that reserves fixed feed positions for underrepresented categories or new creators.

scenario: 有内容违反政策(未成年人不宜、错误信息)，但排序模型偏偏给它打了很高的分。
scenario_en: A piece of content violates policy (age-restricted, misinformation), yet the ranker gives it a very high score.
q: 硬性政策合规该放在哪一层、怎么实现，才能保证不被模型分数覆盖？
q_en: Where and how should hard policy compliance be enforced so a model score can never override it?
why: 政策合规是硬约束，要用重排层里确定性的过滤逻辑强制移除，模型分数无论多高都不能覆盖；把它做成标量化里的负权重是软的，会被更高分盖过。
why_en: Policy compliance is a hard constraint enforced by deterministic filter logic in re-ranking that no score can override; folding it into scalarization as a negative weight is soft and can be outscored.
tradeoff: 确定性硬过滤(绝对但一刀切) vs 标量化负权重(灵活但可能被高分盖过)
options: 用重排层里确定性的硬过滤逻辑移除，模型分数不可覆盖
在标量化打分里给违规内容加一个大负权重，让它自然排到后面
训练时把违规样本标成负例，靠模型自己学会不推
交给召回层，用 ANN 相似度阈值把违规内容挡在候选之外
options_en: Enforce it with deterministic hard-filter logic in the re-ranking layer that no model score can override.
Add a large negative weight to violating content in the scalarized score so it naturally sinks.
Label violating samples as negatives in training and rely on the model to learn not to push them.
Delegate to retrieval, using an ANN similarity threshold to keep violating content out of candidates.
whenOtherWins: 若约束只是「倾向少推」而非「绝不出现」(如轻度降低争议内容)，用标量化里的软性降权更灵活。
optionExplanations: 对；只有确定性硬过滤能保证「绝不出现」，模型分数再高也一票否决。
负权重是软的：一个足够高的相关性分数仍可能把它顶上来，达不到绝不出现。
模型是概率的，学到的偏好不是保证；总有漏网样本被打高分推出去。
召回相似度阈值抓不住政策语义，会误杀也会漏放，不是合规的可靠闸门。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — only a deterministic hard filter guarantees 'never appears', vetoing regardless of how high the score is.
A negative weight is soft: a high enough relevance score can still surface it, failing the never-appear rule.
The model is probabilistic; a learned preference is not a guarantee, and some samples still score high and slip through.
A retrieval similarity threshold cannot capture policy semantics—it both over-blocks and leaks, an unreliable compliance gate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由明确规则(而非模型概率)判定是否移除，结果可复现、可审计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deterministic filter removes items by explicit rules rather than model probability, giving reproducible, auditable outcomes.

scenario: 突发新闻期间，平台希望把权威新闻源顶到 feed 前列，压过普通推荐分数。
scenario_en: During breaking news, the platform wants authoritative news sources boosted to the top of the feed, overriding ordinary recommendation scores.
q: 「突发事件加权权威来源」最该怎么实现？
q_en: How should 'boost authoritative sources during breaking events' be implemented?
why: 这是硬约束里的 position override：用确定性规则在重排阶段把权威来源强制置顶，不依赖模型重新学习或重训，才能即时、可控地响应突发事件。
why_en: This is a hard-constraint position override: deterministic re-ranking rules force authoritative sources to the top, not relying on model retraining, giving immediate controllable response.
tradeoff: 确定性 position override(即时可控) vs 重训模型(慢且不精确)
options: 紧急重训模型，把权威来源的历史点击率调高再上线
在标量化里临时给新闻类目加正权重，等事件过去再撤
在重排阶段用确定性规则把权威来源置顶
扩大召回候选集，多召回一些新闻视频交给排序自然处理
options_en: Urgently retrain the model with authoritative sources' historical CTR boosted, then redeploy.
Temporarily add a positive weight to the news category in scalarization and remove it after the event.
Use a deterministic rule in re-ranking to pin authoritative sources to the top.
Widen the retrieval candidate set to pull in more news videos and let ranking handle it naturally.
whenOtherWins: 若不是突发、而是长期想略微提升某类内容，用标量化里的软加权更平滑，不必硬置顶。
optionExplanations: 重训要数小时到数天，突发新闻等不起，且历史 CTR 反映不了刚发生的事件。
软加权可能被更高相关性盖过，也不保证权威来源一定置顶，响应不够确定。
对；规则写死在 serving 配置里，改一行几分钟就生效，而且谁在何时置顶了什么都可审计。
多召回不保证排到前面，排序仍按分数走，达不到「突发时强制置顶」。
optionExplanations_en: Retraining takes hours to days—breaking news cannot wait—and historical CTR does not reflect a just-happened event.
A soft weight can be outscored by higher relevance and does not guarantee the top slot, too uncertain a response.
Correct — the rule lives in serving config, takes minutes to flip, and leaves an auditable trail of who pinned what and when.
More candidates does not guarantee top placement; ranking still follows score, failing the forced-top requirement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用确定性规则强制某类内容占据指定位置，覆盖模型打分排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A position override forces certain content into designated positions via deterministic rules, overriding model-scored order.

scenario: 历史参与度数据里多数群体创作者互动更多，模型直接学这份数据。
scenario_en: Historical engagement data has majority-demographic creators interacting more, and the model learns straight from it.
q: 把历史参与度偏差自我强化、伤害欠代表创作者的循环排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the loop by which historical engagement bias self-reinforces and harms underrepresented creators:
steps: 模型放大偏差：欠代表创作者被打更低分
更少曝光带来更少互动数据
数据更稀疏使下一轮打分更低，形成强化环
why: 偏差循环：模型放大历史偏差→欠代表创作者打分低→曝光少→数据更少→打分更低。它是自我强化的，所以公平必须在设计期就介入，不能事后审计。
why_en: The bias loop: the model amplifies historical bias, underrepresented creators score lower, get fewer impressions, generate less data, and score even lower—self-reinforcing, so fairness must be designed in, not audited later.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["模型放大偏差
欠代表创作者低分"] --> B["更少曝光"] B --> C["更少互动数据"] C --> D["数据更稀疏→打分更低"] D --> A

termDefinitions.meaning: 历史互动数据偏向多数群体，模型学后进一步放大不平等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Engagement bias is historical interaction data favoring majority groups, which the model then amplifies into greater inequality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条内容被展示给用户一次，是分配注意力的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is one display of content to a user, the basic unit of attention allocation.

scenario: 欠代表创作者质量与他人相当，却因历史偏差长期曝光不足，想在系统里纠正。
scenario_en: Underrepresented creators are comparable in quality but chronically under-exposed due to historical bias, and you want to correct it in-system.
q: 曝光公平(exposure fairness)该在哪里、怎么落地？
q_en: Where and how should exposure fairness be implemented?
why: 在重排阶段加曝光公平约束：按目录占比(catalog share)或约定标准分配曝光份额，而不是纯按预测参与度分配，这样能主动打破「低分→少曝光」的强化环。
why_en: Add an exposure-fairness constraint in re-ranking that allocates impression share by catalog share (or an agreed criterion) rather than purely by predicted engagement, breaking the reinforcing loop.
tradeoff: 按目录占比分配曝光(长期生态健康) vs 纯按预测参与度(短期指标高但强化偏差)
options: 在重排里按目录占比分配曝光份额，而不是纯按预测参与度
在损失函数里删掉所有涉及创作者人群的特征，做到「不看即公平」
维持纯参与度排序，等偏差自己随时间消失
只在年度审计时手工提一批欠代表创作者的排名
options_en: In re-ranking, allocate impression share by catalog share rather than purely by predicted engagement.
Delete every creator-demographic feature from the loss to be 'fair by blindness'.
Keep pure engagement ranking and wait for the bias to fade on its own over time.
Manually bump a batch of underrepresented creators' ranks only during the annual audit.
whenOtherWins: 若某群体是因内容质量真的差而非历史偏差被压，强行按占比给曝光会推低质内容，此时该先修质量信号而非配额。
optionExplanations: 对；曝光公平约束在重排主动分配份额，直接打断「少曝光→少数据→更低分」的强化环。
删特征做不到公平：偏差藏在相关代理特征里，「不看」反而失去纠偏和审计的抓手。
偏差是自我强化的，放任只会越来越糟，不会自己消失。
年度手工提名不可扩展、不可复现，纠不了每天数十亿次的曝光分配。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — an exposure-fairness constraint in re-ranking actively allocates share, directly breaking the 'less exposure → less data → lower score' loop.
Deleting features is not fairness: bias hides in correlated proxy features, and blindness loses the lever to correct and audit.
Bias is self-reinforcing; leaving it alone makes it worse, not better on its own.
Annual manual nominations do not scale and are irreproducible, unable to fix billions of daily impression allocations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让不同创作者群体获得与其目录占比或约定标准相称的曝光份额。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exposure fairness gives creator groups an impression share proportional to their catalog share or an agreed criterion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某群体内容在全站可推物料中所占的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Catalog share is the fraction of the recommendable corpus that a group's content makes up.

scenario: 要检查模型是否系统性低估某些创作者群体，而不只看整体指标。
scenario_en: You need to check whether the model systematically under-scores certain creator groups, not just look at aggregate metrics.
q: 公平性的 calibration audit(校准审计)具体查什么？
q_en: What exactly does a fairness calibration audit check?
why: 校准审计按创作者人群(性别/地域/语言)切片看预测分：在质量可比时若某群体分数被系统性压低，就是模型放大了偏差，需要纠偏。
why_en: It slices predictions by creator demographic (gender/geography/language) and checks whether a group's scores are systematically lower despite comparable quality.
options: 只看全站平均观看时长有没有上涨
按创作者人群切片看预测分是否被系统性压低
统计模型总参数量是否超过部署预算
检查 ANN 索引的召回率是否达标
options_en: Just check whether site-wide average watch time went up.
Slice predicted scores by creator demographic and check for systematic under-scoring.
Count whether total model parameters exceed the deployment budget.
Check whether the ANN index's recall meets target.
optionExplanations: 全站均值会掩盖群体间差异——总量涨了也可能某群体被系统性压低。
对；切片对比是发现「同质量不同分」的唯一办法，正是校准审计的核心动作。
参数量是部署成本问题，和群体公平无关。
召回率是召回质量指标，查不出创作者群体间的打分偏差。
optionExplanations_en: A site-wide mean masks between-group gaps—the total can rise while one group is systematically suppressed.
Correct — sliced comparison is the only way to spot 'same quality, different score', the heart of a calibration audit.
Parameter count is a deployment-cost concern, unrelated to group fairness.
Recall is a retrieval-quality metric and cannot reveal scoring bias across creator groups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按人群切片对比预测分，检查是否在质量可比时系统性偏低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A calibration audit slices predictions by group to check for systematically lower scores at comparable quality.

scenario: 团队争论公平性该是上线前跑一次的审计，还是持续监控的一等指标。
scenario_en: The team debates whether fairness is a one-off pre-launch audit or a continuously monitored first-class metric.
q: Staff+ 会怎么对待公平性在系统里的地位？
q_en: How would a Staff+ engineer position fairness in the system?
why: 把公平当作被监控的 SLO：一块 dashboard 同时看参与度(观看时长/CTR)和公平(按人群的曝光份额、校准曲线)，配告警。公平是持续监控对象，不是上线后一次性审计。
why_en: Treat fairness as a monitored SLO: one dashboard tracks engagement (watch time/CTR) and fairness (impression share by demographic, calibration curves) side by side with alerts, not a one-off audit.
tradeoff: 公平作为持续监控 SLO(可及时纠偏) vs 一次性上线审计(易回退失守)
options: 上线前做一次公平审计，通过后就不再监控
把公平当被监控的 SLO，配 dashboard 告警
只在用户投诉时临时查一次相关群体的排名
把公平完全交给法务合规，工程侧不设指标
options_en: Do one fairness audit before launch and stop monitoring once it passes.
Treat fairness as a monitored SLO with a dashboard and alerts.
Only spot-check some group's ranking when users complain.
Hand fairness entirely to legal compliance, with no engineering metric.
whenOtherWins: 若产品还在 MVP、量级极小且无公平风险敞口，可先只做上线前抽查，等规模上来再建持续监控。
optionExplanations: 一次性审计会随模型迭代和数据漂移失守，偏差会悄悄回来却没人发现。
对；持续监控 + 告警才能在偏差回潮时及时发现纠正，公平是活的指标不是一次通过。
等投诉太被动，很多被压制的群体根本没有发声渠道，问题长期隐藏。
公平既是合规也是工程问题，没有工程指标就无法监控和迭代。
optionExplanations_en: A one-off audit lapses as the model iterates and data drifts; bias quietly returns unnoticed.
Correct — continuous monitoring plus alerts catches bias regressions in time; fairness is a live metric, not a one-time pass.
Waiting for complaints is too passive; many suppressed groups have no channel to speak up and the problem stays hidden.
Fairness is both a compliance and an engineering problem; without an engineering metric you cannot monitor or iterate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某项指标设定的目标阈值，持续监控并在越界时告警。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a target threshold for a metric, continuously monitored with alerts on breach.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击数除以曝光数，衡量内容吸引点击的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is clicks divided by impressions, measuring how often content is clicked.

scenario: A/B 显示纯观看时长排序器 +12% 观看时长，但 +15% 用户不满(dissatisfaction，来自不喜欢/调查)。
scenario_en: An A/B shows a watch-time-only ranker gains +12% watch time but +15% dissatisfaction (from dislikes/surveys).
q: 面对这个结果，最该做的一步改动是什么？
q_en: Given this result, what is the single best change to make?
why: 观看时长涨但不满也涨，是典型单目标 cannibalization。最直接的修法是加一个满意度预测头(如点赞率/调查分)并把它并入标量化打分，用满意度对冲纯观看时长。
why_en: Rising watch time with rising dissatisfaction is classic single-objective cannibalization; add a satisfaction prediction head and fold it into the scalarized score to offset raw watch time.
tradeoff: 加满意度头对冲(牺牲一点观看时长换满意) vs 只追观看时长(短期指标高但用户流失)
options: 加一个满意度预测头，并入标量化打分
直接上线这个版本，因为观看时长是主指标、+12% 够好
把观看时长权重再调高，让指标涨得更多
彻底放弃观看时长目标，只用点赞率排序
options_en: Add a satisfaction prediction head and fold it into the scalarized score.
Ship this version, since watch time is the primary metric and +12% is good enough.
Raise the watch-time weight further so the metric climbs even more.
Abandon the watch-time objective entirely and rank by like rate only.
whenOtherWins: 若不满上升只是新鲜效应(novelty)导致的短期噪声、跑满 1–2 周后回落，则可能无需加头，先观察再决定。
optionExplanations: 对；加满意度头把「人不满」变成可优化信号并入打分，正面对冲观看时长的副作用。
+15% 不满会侵蚀长期留存；只盯主指标就上线，等于拿长期用户信任换短期曲线。
调高观看时长权重会让不满更严重，方向完全反了。
只用点赞率会丢掉观看深度信号，从一个极端跳到另一个极端。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a satisfaction head turns 'users are dissatisfied' into an optimizable signal folded into scoring, directly offsetting watch time's side effect.
A +15% dissatisfaction rate erodes long-term retention; shipping on the headline metric alone trades user trust for a short-term curve.
Raising the watch-time weight worsens dissatisfaction—exactly the wrong direction.
Ranking by like rate alone drops watch-depth signal, swinging from one extreme to the other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 优化一个指标系统性拖垮另一个，如观看时长涨但满意度掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cannibalization is when optimizing one metric systematically degrades another, e.g. watch time up but satisfaction down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对任何新东西短期都更爱互动，会误导 A/B 结论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The novelty effect is users engaging more with anything new short-term, which can mislead A/B conclusions.

scenario: 把「从单目标排序升级到多目标排序」这个决策讲成一条完整链路。
scenario_en: Explain the decision to upgrade from single- to multi-objective ranking as one complete chain.
q: 把多目标排序的决策链排成正确顺序(需求→性质→选择→代价→缓解)：
q_en: Order the multi-objective ranking decision chain (requirement → property → choice → cost → mitigation):
steps: 需求：不能只追观看时长，要同时兼顾满意度/新鲜度/多样性
关键性质：需要显式、可优化的满意度信号来对冲
选择：共享 backbone + 多预测头，用标量化合成一个分
代价：多个权重不是常数、难人工设定
缓解：用在线 A/B 按 surface 调权，并设 guardrail 监控
why: 链路：先说需求(别单极)→点出关键性质(要显式满意度信号)→选多头+标量化→承认代价(权重难定)→给缓解(A/B 调权 + guardrail)。面试里这样一条链能体现取舍思维。
why_en: The chain: state the requirement (no single objective), name the property (need an explicit satisfaction signal), choose multi-head plus scalarization, admit the cost (weights are hard to set), and mitigate with per-surface A/B tuning plus guardrails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不被直接优化但不能恶化的指标(如不喜欢率)，越线就叫停实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is not optimized directly but must not regress (e.g. dislike rate); breaching it kills the experiment.

scenario: 排序模型已给几百候选打好分，要经过重排后处理再展示。
scenario_en: The ranker has scored a few hundred candidates; they pass through re-ranking post-processing before display.
q: 把重排后处理的执行顺序排对：
q_en: Put the re-ranking post-processing steps in the correct order:
steps: 拿到排序模型的标量化分数列表
注入软性多样性(MMR / 槽位规则)重新组织顺序
施加硬性政策/安全过滤，移除违规内容
why: 顺序：先拿排序分→软性多样化(MMR/槽位)调整顺序→硬性政策/安全过滤兜底移除→出最终列表。软的可权衡放前面，硬的一票否决放最后确保没有违规漏出。
why_en: Order: take the scored list, inject soft diversity (MMR/slots), apply hard policy/safety filters, then output; soft trade-offs go first and the hard veto goes last to guarantee nothing violating slips through.
diagram:
flowchart LR S["排序分数列表"] --> D["软性多样化
MMR/槽位"] D --> P["硬性政策/安全过滤"] P --> O["最终展示列表"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 重排末端的确定性关卡，移除违规/不安全内容，模型分数不可覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A safety filter is a deterministic gate at the end of re-ranking that removes violating/unsafe content, unoverridable by model score.

scenario: 除了算法层的多样化，产品侧也能给用户直接的控制权来减小信息茧房。
scenario_en: Beyond algorithmic diversity, the product side can hand users direct controls to reduce filter bubbles.
q: 哪种产品侧手段能直接让用户减小自己的信息茧房深度？
q_en: Which product-side lever lets users directly reduce their own filter-bubble depth?
why: 用户控制项(「少推这类」按钮、话题滑块)让用户显式表达不想看什么，直接降低茧房深度，是算法多样化之外的产品杠杆。
why_en: User controls ('show me less of this', topic sliders) let users explicitly say what they don't want, directly reducing filter-bubble depth alongside algorithmic diversity.
options: 把所有用户的推荐权重设成一样，抹平个性化
提供「少推这类」按钮和话题滑块
把召回候选集缩小，减少用户能看到的内容种类
关闭个性化，所有人改看同一份纯热门榜
options_en: Set all users' recommendation weights identical, flattening personalization.
Offer a 'show me less of this' button and topic sliders.
Shrink the retrieval candidate set so users see fewer kinds of content.
Turn off personalization so everyone sees the same trending chart.
optionExplanations: 抹平个性化会损害相关性，也不是「让用户控制」，方向不对。
对；用户控制项把多样化的选择权交给用户本人，直接、可解释地减小茧房。
缩小候选集反而减少多样性来源，与目标相反。
纯热门榜牺牲个性化且未必更多样，不是给用户控制权。
optionExplanations_en: Flattening personalization hurts relevance and is not 'user control', the wrong direction.
Correct — user controls hand the diversification choice to the user, directly and interpretably shrinking the bubble.
Shrinking candidates reduces diversity sources, the opposite of the goal.
A pure trending chart sacrifices personalization and is not necessarily more diverse, nor does it give users control.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让用户显式表达偏好的产品功能，如「少推这类」按钮、话题滑块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: User controls are product features letting users state preferences explicitly, like a 'show less' button or topic sliders.
